# Intake and Output Record — Keiko Sato
Clearwater Skilled Nursing Center | 04/18/2026 | 3:00 PM–11:00 PM
Resident: Keiko Sato | Room 214 | Nurse: Paul Kowalczyk, LPN

## Shift measurements
All fluid amounts are recorded in mL. Oral intake was measured at the bedside; urine was measured from the indwelling catheter drainage bag.

| Time | Intake | Output | Details |
| --- | ---: | ---: | --- |
| 4:00 PM | 240 | 300 | Water; urine |
| 6:00 PM | 180 | 250 | Broth; urine |
| 8:00 PM | 240 | 200 | Tea; urine |
| 10:00 PM | 120 | 300 | Water; urine |
| Total | 780 | 1,050 | Shift totals |

## Nursing note
Resident awake and able to drink without assistance. Intake includes all fluids consumed during the shift; no IV fluids were administered. Urine was pale yellow and without visible sediment. At 7:15 PM, I disconnected catheter tubing to pour urine into a graduated cylinder, then reconnected it. Resident denied discomfort. No emesis or liquid stool occurred during the shift.

The shift summary records 780 mL intake and 1,250 mL output. Reported totals were given to Tyrone Gallagher, RN, at 11:00 PM. Continue measuring and recording each intake and output event on the next shift. Keiko remained in bed with call light within reach at handoff.

errors.quote: I disconnected catheter tubing to pour urine
errors.explanation: A urinary catheter drainage system should remain closed; disconnecting the tubing breaks the closed system and increases infection risk. Urine can be measured from the drainage bag without disconnecting the tubing.
errors.fix: I measured urine from the drainage bag without disconnecting catheter tubing

errors.quote: records 780 mL intake and 1,250 mL output
errors.explanation: The table lists outputs of 300, 250, 200, and 300 mL, totaling 1,050 mL, and the table’s shift total confirms that amount. The narrative’s output total is inconsistent.
errors.fix: records 780 mL intake and 1,050 mL output
